justice: The allocation of multiple wide asphalt lanes for motor vehicles compared to visually marginalized peripheral paths shows poor equity in spatial distribution for pedestrians and cyclists
The excessive crossing distance of the multi-lane road creates significant barriers for older adults and persons with disabilities, reducing accessibility
The lack of visible pedestrian refuge islands or tactile paving in the roadway design compromises fairness for visually and mobility impaired users
safety: Overhead pedestrian crossing warning signs provide necessary visual cues for drivers to watch out for vulnerable road users
The physical separation provided by the continuous green hedge on the right protects cyclists and pedestrians from direct conflict with high-speed vehicle traffic
The wide, straight motor vehicle lanes encourage high driving speeds, significantly increasing the risk and severity of potential accidents involving teenagers or elderly pedestrians
livability: The complete absence of ground-floor commercial facades or residential buildings results in an environment lacking social vitality for all age groups
The prominent large industrial pipeline on the right and high-voltage power lines on the left create a barren atmosphere unsuitable for community interaction
There are no visible public gathering spaces or active frontages, restricting opportunities for older adults and teenagers to engage in street-level social life
sustainability: The extensive impermeable asphalt surface of the wide roadway increases urban heat island effects and surface water runoff
Green hedges and mature trees along both sides of the road provide some ecological value and carbon absorption
The highly car-centric road design lacks visible public transit infrastructure like bus stops, failing to encourage low-carbon travel for vulnerable social groups
aesthetics: The modern cable-stayed bridge in the distance serves as a strong visual landmark and focal point for drivers and active commuters
Prominent high-voltage transmission towers and overhead wires on the left side negatively impact the visual harmony and skyline of the streetscape
The continuous green planting strip along the right side offers a pleasant natural visual break from the extensive gray pavement
comfort: The wide, unshaded expanse of asphalt offers no thermal comfort or canopy protection for pedestrians or cyclists during hot weather
The complete lack of street furniture, such as benches along the visible paths, severely limits physical comfort for elderly pedestrians needing to rest
The sheer scale of the high-speed traffic lanes and industrial infrastructure creates a psychologically intimidating and stressful environment for socially vulnerable groups
walkability: The massive width of the multi-lane road creates intimidating and exhaustingly long crossing distances for older adults and children
Pedestrian pathways are pushed to the extreme edges behind barriers, reducing direct route connectivity and walking convenience
The lack of human-scale street lighting and pedestrian-oriented street furniture makes walking feel isolated and physically demanding
bikeability: The presence of a physically separated path behind the right-side planting strip provides a basic level of safety for cyclists away from fast cars
The vast, car-dominated intersections and lack of clear bicycle lane markings pose significant navigation risks for younger or elderly cyclists
The entirely car-scaled infrastructure lacks supporting micro-mobility facilities, such as visible bicycle parking or dedicated wayfinding signage
